verdict.rationale: Codex's docs describe the core loop: start in a repository, plan a change, edit files and run tools locally (codex-docs-9, codex-docs-30, codex-docs-8). You can also start work from GitHub or Linear issues and Slack threads, then review a diff or open a PR (codex-docs-2, codex-docs-5, codex-docs-6). Hands-on community reports back this up, e.g. it "fixes everything in 3 minutes" and is "shockingly good", though one user says it "struggles with … almost anything" (codex-comm-14, codex-comm-18, codex-comm-8, codex-comm-3). Missing for 10: no explicit documentation of coordinated multi-file edits, and no first-party walkthrough of turning a plain-language feature or bug description into an implementation.
